parameters.content:
## 06 VDR Weekly Vendor Disposition Report
Each vendor gets a weekly CSV of every lead it provided in the last 90 days (by LP entry date) with the lead's current LP status and sale amount.

**Feed:** LP emails report 135 Lead Disposition Detail 2 daily to lp-reports@ with subject **Reece Vendor Disposition Feed** (d5=ALL, t1=DAYOFFSET(-90), t2=DAYOFFSET(0)). Keep this subject distinct: I.LPRC watches "Lead Disposition Detail" and 05 watches "Reece Daily Aged Leads Update".

**Vendor settings:** table `vdr_vendor_config` (LP Supabase). One row per vendor: LP sub-sources, recipients To/CC, send day (1=Mon) and time, active, dry_run, lookback days. Add / pause / remove a vendor there; no workflow change.

**One trigger (Mark, 2026-10-14):** the run starts when the feed email lands (Gmail trigger, same inbox and credential as 05 LF, polled hourly) and the report is built from THAT email (Feed email (from trigger)). No timer, no second search: on a non-send day the run finds nobody due and ends quietly; a blocked or failed vendor is retried by the NEXT day's feed email (Mon, Tue, Wed = the 3 attempts). Vendor send time is 00:00, so Monday's ~6:30 AM feed sends. Manual test: open the Gmail trigger, Fetch Test Event, Execute workflow. On 2026-10-14 the LP schedule was named "Lead Disposition Detail Last 90 Days": the old search found nothing (no_feed_email) AND I.LPRC would have ingested the 90-day file as the daily 135 report. The subject must stay "Reece Vendor Disposition Feed".

**Due:** `rpc/vdr_due_vendors` returns active vendors whose send slot this PERIOD has passed and that have no sent/no-leads row this period (blocked/failed retried by the next feed email, max 3 per period).

**Frequency (Mark, 2026-10-14):** per vendor, `frequency` = weekly (the first feed email on or after Monday 00:00) or monthly (the first feed email on or after the 1st at 00:00), set on the dashboard's Vendor Reports page. `week_start` in vdr_send_log is the PERIOD start (Monday, or the 1st). A vendor switched weekly -> monthly after a Monday send is not sent again that month; monthly -> weekly after a 1st-of-month send waits for the next Monday.

**Checks (fail closed, nothing sent):** feed email missing or older than 26h, required columns missing, rows without lead id or entry date, feed window shorter than lookback, feed < 70% of last good feed, live vendor with no recipients, and a per-vendor reconcile (every lead id in the window appears exactly once).

**One row per lead:** current row beats Superseded, then newest entry date. All dispositions included (Sale, DNC, Remove too).

**Log:** `vdr_send_log` (one row per vendor per attempt). Mark gets one summary email per run listing what was sent (Mark, 2026-10-14: no list of LP sub-sources without a vendor; `feed_info.unmapped` still exists in the Build output for anyone who needs it).

**DRY RUN** is per vendor (`dry_run` column). true = report goes to Mark only. Built 2026-10-13.

**REV SHARE (2026-10-13).** A vendor with `rev_share=true` (LeadPilot, Contractor Appointment Rev Share) is paid per job RELEASED TO PRODUCTION, so it also gets **Payable Jobs**: every job from its sub-sources whose RTP date fell in the PRIOR Sunday..Saturday pay period (job #, sale amount, job status), as a second CSV, and its lead CSV gains Job # / Released to Production Date. Data: `rpc/vdr_rev_share_data` — lp_job_milestones (datetype RTP, act_date::date) joined to 133 Jobs By Status (`lp_job_status_history`, latest row per job) by JOB ID; the 135 lead id is job_status.lp_id. Never join milestones.lp_lead_id to a 135 id (different id space); it is only the fallback through lp_jobs -> lp_leads to attribute an RTP job 133 has not reported yet.
**Ledger:** `vdr_payable_jobs`, one row per job actually emailed, unique (vendor_id, lp_job_id, dry_run): a job is listed once, ever (dry run and live separately). Already-listed jobs are skipped and counted in the summary.
**Rev-share blocks (that vendor only):** rtp_data_stale (milestones not synced in 24h), job_status_data_stale (no 133 contract in 3 days), rtp_jobs_without_source (an RTP job in the period that is this vendor's by LP lead source but missing from 133, or has no source at all), rev_share_data_unavailable. Zero payable jobs is valid: lead report still goes, body says so, no empty CSV. Cancelled-looking payable jobs are sent and flagged in Mark's summary, never dropped.

nodes.name: Get rev-share data
nodes.notes: Rev share (2026-10-13): per active rev-share vendor the prior Sun..Sat pay period, its payable jobs (lp_job_milestones RTP x 133 Jobs By Status by job id), every RTP of its jobs, and the health facts the build fails closed on.

nodes.name: Write payable ledger
nodes.notes: One vdr_payable_jobs row per payable job whose email went out. The unique index (vendor_id, lp_job_id, dry_run) + ignore-duplicates means a job can never be listed twice.
